portInfo.description: Castries concentrates Saint Lucia’s cruise traffic. SLASPA describes Pointe Seraphine as a dedicated cruise shopping and berth complex within walking distance of the city, with La Place Carenage serving ships at the Queen Elizabeth II docks and water taxis linking the retail hubs. The commercial Saint Lucia Cruise Port site lists Pointe Seraphine berth lengths and draught figures plus larger numbered berths. Berth tables differ between sources — confirm your assigned terminal and gangway with the cruise line before planning transfers.

climate.description: Tropical climate with warm temperatures year-round

politics.visaRequirements: Visa-free for many nationalities (up to 90 days).
politics.entryRequirements: Valid passport required. Return ticket may be required.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Pointe Seraphine / Saint Lucia Cruise Port (Castries) — Castries, Saint Lucia
gettingThere.distanceToCity: The downtown market area is a short walk from the cruise terminals — keep time for crowds at the gangway. Soufrière and the Pitons are full-day coach outings; allow at least two hours’ buffer beyond advertised tour length.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Castries market — check opening hours locally on your call day.
Pointe Seraphine / La Place Carenage shopping
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Ask which berth number you are on — Castries can host multiple ships.
